precepts.text: Though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more. And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it. That word that you hear is how you are born of the spirit.
precepts.point: The wind bloweth where it listeth: that wind blowing where it will is the word of God. You do not know who the word of God is going to affect. Thou hearest the sound thereof: we heard this truth, we heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth; you hear a certain word and you wake up. So is every one that is born of the Spirit.

note.label: Born for Adversity

precepts.why:
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” Christ says “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” What is that really saying? Isaiah shows it.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.” That word you hear, this is the way, walk ye in it, is how you are born. That is how you are born of the spirit.

The wind that blows where it will is the word of God. You don't know who the word of God is going to affect. The sound thereof is “This is the way, walk ye in it”, the word of God. Every last one of us in here heard the truth, heard that sound, heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth, like sleeper cells: you just hear a certain trigger word behind you and you activate, you wake up to this truth. The Bible is the activation.

And notice what comes with it: the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. A brother is born for adversity. When you are born into this truth and depart from evil, you make yourself a prey; Satan comes for you, and you will have to go through things. But the teachers are no longer hid in a corner, and the word behind you keeps you walking in the way.

precepts.text: He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already. And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. They hate Christ and the commandments because coming to the light reproves the deeds. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God. We want the word of God to make our deeds manifest: Lord, show me what I am.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

precepts.text: Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
precepts.point: The Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt be turned into another man. You don't believe that you could become a whole different person; the scripture says you can.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.text: After the civil rights era Christianity changed from the Klan's white Jesus to God loves everybody and all-inclusive churches; the lamb's horns and the dragon's voice, a doctrine of adaptation, while the truth cannot adapt.
precepts.point: The 1960s and the 1990s were the two waves: the truth began in 1969 and the one-West teachers came in the 1990s, so Esau hit each wave with the Bible revisions, the vaccine schedule, crack, the three-strikes law and the prison pipeline.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The plan said the old religions will have to go, and that goes into Christianity itself changing. Before the civil rights movement, Christianity was used to oppress us. A lot of the KKK were Christians. The white man would tell you straight that he was worshipping white Jesus and lynching you, and that you could not pray for him; you couldn't go to a white church. White people were just conquering and destroying everybody.

After the civil rights era they started changing Christianity up. Now they started implementing John 3:16, and Galatians, and saying everybody can go to heaven and God loves everybody. Christianity became all-inclusive, and it was not like that sixty years ago.

That goes back to Revelation, the beast with two horns like a lamb that spake as a dragon. The same people who taught the old white Christianity changed the face of it, but the voice is still the dragon's. It is the same trick as civil rights: the ostensible purpose is that black people get their rights, and the real purpose is rights for every heathen to exploit us, while black schools and black businesses that were thriving fail.

Christianity is a doctrine of adaptation, and so the white man's religion adapted when it needed to. The truth cannot adapt. That is how Daniel 7:25 is fulfilled: he thinks to change times and laws, and even the teaching of his religion is changed to keep our people from the laws and commandments of God.

precepts.text: This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

precepts.text: Men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. There are people who were ordained of old to stay like that; God gave them up to strong delusion, and some people are bound in that darkness.
precepts.point: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh: other nations, and worse, as it is today. They are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire: that lake of fire we read about in Revelation 14.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Jude says the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved “in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” Has that great day come yet, brothers? No. Those sons of God who went in unto the daughters of men were destroyed in the flood, and those spirits came right back, by way of the three sons, Ham, Shem and Japheth. They are still here today.

John shows what that darkness is: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men loving darkness rather than light is sin: you hate God's laws, you hate this truth, you hate the Bible.

There are people like that who were ordained of old to stay like that, the “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. Remember 2 Thessalonians: God gave them up to strong delusion, that they should believe a lie and not repent and come into the light. Some people are bound in that darkness, and there is nothing you can do for them. That is the chains of darkness, reserved unto the judgment of the great day.

precepts.text: Nicodemus, a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, came to Christ by night; an Israelite came to an Israelite.
precepts.point: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

note.label: Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass

precepts.why:
Christ brought the serpent of brass to Nicodemus. “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.”

Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: an Israelite came to an Israelite. Two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel, the fiery serpents that bit the people and the serpent of brass on the pole.

precepts.text: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish.
precepts.point: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

note.label: Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass

precepts.why:
Moses “made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.” Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. That brass serpent was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture.

Christ told Nicodemus, “And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.”

As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. The serpent healed Israel; the Son of man lifted up saves Israel.

precepts.text: This is one of those lies learned under the false image, telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” This is one of those lies learned under the false image, the teacher of lies: telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.

That is what the graven image teaches. The psalm says our God is in the heavens and his glory is not unto us but unto his name, for his mercy and for his truth's sake, and they that trust in the image are like unto it.

precepts.text: The wind bloweth where it listeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit. The word rests on those it is given to.
precepts.point: Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance; but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” The mysteries are given to some and not to others. “For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.”

Christ told Nicodemus how that works: “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” The wind goes where it will, and you cannot say where it comes from or where it goes; so is every one born of the Spirit. The word rests on those it is given to. That is why it is given to the disciples to know the mysteries and not to the others, and why the one who has receives more while the one who has not loses even what he has.

precepts.text: He gave his only begotten Son. A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face.
precepts.point: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” The Word was made flesh, and we beheld his glory, “the glory as of the only begotten of the Father”; here Christ says whose only begotten Son that is. God gave his Son.

A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face. The Father gave; the Son was given. The Word made flesh that dwelt among us, full of grace and truth, is the only begotten Son of the Father, not the Father himself.

precepts.text: If so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive, and after death ye shall obtain mercy.
precepts.point: This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. And Christ told him, “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Ezra gives the same thing: “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.” To be born again, a man has to subdue his own understanding and reform his heart.

Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over. Subdue your own understanding, and you shall be kept alive, and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.text: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
precepts.point: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus took it literally and asked whether a man can “enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born”. Christ answered, “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.”

Peter tells what that birth is: “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” Being born again is by the word of God. Both the water and the Spirit are named plainly elsewhere as the word. It is not a second birth from a mother's womb; it is a birth of incorruptible seed, the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

precepts.text: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
precepts.point: A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.” Paul draws the line: “So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.”

A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles. That which is born of the flesh stays flesh, and they that are in the flesh cannot please God. That is why Christ says, “Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” A man must be born of the Spirit to please God.

precepts.text: Much people of Israel died, and every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
precepts.point: The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up”. The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. “And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.”

“And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.” It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten. “Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.”

“And the Lord said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.” It was Israel that looked and lived. Even so the Son of man was lifted up, “That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life”: the same people, bitten, looking, and living.

precepts.text: They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
precepts.point: The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Solomon tells what the serpent of brass was: “For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever: But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.”

The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it. They had said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord”, and the sign put them in remembrance of the commandment of the law.

So when the Son of man is lifted up like that serpent, believing in him goes with the same thing: remembrance of the commandment of the law, and repentance.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; that he should be made manifest to Israel.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son”. This follows straight on from the serpent lifted up in the wilderness for Israel, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is.

John the Baptist said, “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Then he said why he came: “And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.” The Lamb that takes away the sin of the world was to be made manifest to Israel. The world whose sin he takes away is the one he was made manifest to: Israel.

precepts.text: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.”

Much people came to the feast and cried out that he is the King of Israel. That multitude was Israel, and it is that same multitude the Pharisees are speaking of next when they say the world is gone after him. So the world in “God so loved the world” is that people, the ones who called him the King of Israel.

precepts.text: The Pharisees said, Behold, the world is gone after him, of that same multitude.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.”

The Pharisees said the world is gone after him, of that same multitude that took branches of palm trees and cried, “Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.” That multitude was the world. John's own gospel uses the word that way, so “God so loved the world” is speaking of that people, the same ones the serpent was lifted up for.

Not to receive his testimony is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believes on the Son has the witness in himself, and has set to his seal that God is true; he that believes not has made God a liar. In Acts 2 Peter says whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved, and the very next verse answers who that is: ye men of Israel. Joel said the same, that the Most High is in the midst of Israel and deliverance is in Zion and Jerusalem. The whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands, not all nations.

That is how Philip comes to baptize the eunuch in water. Some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism, even though Christ's baptism is not water. John pointed them to Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people”. The you is Israel. “But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand”.

The Lord loved us not because we were the greatest in number, but because of the oath he made with our forefathers. As a nation our people are vile and evil, and the only reason God has not destroyed us off this planet is the love he had for our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For their sakes we exist. Abraham was a friend of God, and God is a faithful friend: however evil and stupid we have been, he keeps his love for the patriarchs.

So that is the love John 3:16 speaks of. Nowhere in the Old Testament does God love the Moabites or the Canaanites, or make a promise with their forefathers.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“Only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people, as it is this day.”

The Lord delighted in our fathers to love them, and because of that love he chose their seed after them, us, above all people. God loved Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and that love passed on to us. That is what the love of John 3:16 is.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.”

This is twofold. It goes to Christ first and foremost, who fled into Egypt from Herod, prophetically. And it is the Lord loving us: “I loved him.” When did he love us? Because of the promise he made to our forefathers. That is the world that God so loved, and it will be read again and again.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” The Lord always reminded us and our forefathers how he took us out of bondage. He told Abraham he would deliver his seed, and because of the love he had for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and how faithful and righteous they were, that love passed on to us. In Egypt under hard bondage, God remembered the covenant he made with our forefathers.

“When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee”. That is going into Egypt and the deliverance: the Most High used Moses to part the Red Sea, we walked through the middle, and the water did not drown us; he was with us, the chariot over our heads. The rivers are Jordan.

“When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.” Why mention fire? Because the deliverance out of Egypt back then was through the water, and the deliverance out of this Egypt will be through the fire. When the nukes and bombs drop, we will be in the midst of it and not be taken; everyone else will burn and disintegrate. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego walked in the fiery furnace with an angel and nothing touched them: an allegory of what happens to us in this time. Speaking of bombs and missiles: the news showed a Hellfire missile, one of the most destructive there is, hitting a glowing flying object head on, a direct hit, and it bounced off like a ball and kept on going. The elites who run this world know what those things are, and they know they cannot stop them. They are terrified, and they should be, because there will be a bunch of those coming soon. This is war; they are coming for us, Esau, and they are coming for you too, and not the way you think.

“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” He killed the Egyptians to deliver us, and destroyed those too. “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” The thou is Israel. God is saying, I will kill nations for you to save you. Nowhere does he say I will kill Edom for Canaan or Ishmael for Ham. He delivers Israel out of the water and out of the fire, not all nations. Where do you get all nations from?

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi. I have loved you, saith the Lord.” He has always loved us. “Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?” We were always in captivity, always rebellious, always in slavery, so we ask, when did you love us? God answers by returning to the brothers: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau”.

“And laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He gave Esau a mountainous land, and over time had Ishmael remove him out of the land. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: conquered, in the Caucasus mountains, subjugated by Israel. “But we will return and build the desolate places”: that is the Renaissance, when the Italians began to rebuild and reestablish themselves. “They shall build, but I will throw down”: they rise, but he brings them down.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: this nation is the beginning and the end of all evil. All nations are wicked; there are evil vile black and brown devils all over the place, Nino Brown and Frank Lucas on steroids, and we spend more time dealing with them than the heathens. That is who Christ dealt with. Christ did not spend his time arguing with white folk. Meanwhile some of you are still in slavery under him, his face on your money, paying his taxes and his rent, carrying his last name and his license in your wallet, but him kissing your foot gives you solace.

“The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” People say hated means he preferred Esau less. So you tell your twin son, I don’t hate you, I just prefer you less? Damn you Christians are stupid. Indignation is a righteous anger, strong displeasure, and the first synonym given is resentment, and resentment is hatred. Throughout the whole Bible Esau is condemned, slaughtered and destroyed, despised from the moment he was born. There is no place where Edom is granted mercy. So the love of John 3:16 is the love for Jacob, not Esau.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?”

When Christ taught, he taught from Moses and the prophets. The prophets did not sit around negating what Moses said; they built upon the foundation Moses laid. So the words of Moses were the words of Christ. Who do you think gave Moses those laws in the first place? Who was Moses talking to that whole time? Not Christ’s Father: our Father, Christ. We were talking to Dad, and Christ’s Father is Grandpa.

So when we read the words of Moses or the prophets, where do we find him saying he loves all the nations, or that he sent his son to die for all the nations? You will not find it.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” This is six days before the Passover, in Bethany. Everyone knew Lazarus was dead, so they came to see with their own eyes whether he was really alive.

“But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”: black devils, going to kill Lazarus a second time. “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” Keep that in mind: many of the Jews believed on Christ because he raised Lazarus.

Then read on: “For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.” We are losing our following. What world went after Christ because of Lazarus? Were all nations there? Verse 11 tells you: many of the Jews went away and believed. So the Pharisees called the Jews the world. The cosmos. We are the world, and not the Michael Jackson song; the biblical world.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” Israel is a world without end.

Some say that is a mistranslation and the word there is ages without end. No problem: the Pharisees still called Israel the world. And to the heathens in the comments saying nations are going to be saved too: of course you will be saved. Relax. You play a vital role in the kingdom of God, and what that role is comes at the end.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.”

He spoke openly to the world in the synagogue and in the temple, where the Jews always resort. What world was in the temple? Were the Chinese and the Arabs in there? No. So the Pharisees called Israel the world, and Christ called Israel the world. And the word there is the same G2889, kosmos. So Israel is a cosmos.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”. Unto us, Isaiah’s people: a child is begotten, a son is given. That is “he gave his only begotten Son.” “And the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” This son is called the mighty God: Christ is a mighty God. And The everlasting Father, capital F, because he is our Father, our creator, and his Father is his creator. Keep in mind the Prince of Peace: peace between whom? That comes in Ephesians 2.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” He is of Judah, on David’s throne. His government and his order: he orders it and establishes the kingdom of Israel with judgment and justice, not American justice but godly, theocratic justice. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this”: the zeal of the Lord is the word of God.

So the world God so loved is government and order: kosmos, definition one, the harmonious constitution, order and government of the kingdom of Israel.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

precepts.why:
“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The Lord there, in all capitals, is the Father. The righteous Branch is Christ, the same as the root out of a dry ground in Isaiah 53. Judgment and justice: Isaiah 9:7 again.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely”: all twelve tribes in the kingdom. “And this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” The king’s name, not the heavenly Father’s, who is in verse 5. The Son is called by the Father’s title, in all capitals: senior and junior. You love the Hebrew until the Bible comes out, then the confusion starts.

note.label: State of Decay

precepts.why:

“Ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” They will say you have to go to the Greek, the Septuagint, the lexicon, the other translations. The everlasting life of John 3:16 is the everlasting salvation of Israel.

note.label: State of Decay

precepts.why:
Our forefathers understood who the world was. They were not colorblind.

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there”. Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

“For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.” What did the Pharisees call the Jews? The world. They understood who the world was.

Christianity programmed our people to demonize our own heritage and give up our name, identity and tongue to fit into their squares, circles and triangles, to hate ourselves and how we look.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
What is the spirit? A lot of Christians think it is just a puff of smoke that goes inside of you while you do nothing: keep no commandments, keep no laws, just believe and you are full of the spirit. Yeah, of Satan. Of God? No.

“There is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.” A lot of Israelites read the law, read the Bible, and the law accuses them all the time. They commit acts against the laws of God and don’t see it.

“For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Moses wrote of Christ all throughout Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy; you find Christ all through the law. “But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” So the words that Christ spoke were the words of Moses, and the prophets also spoke the words of Moses.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“It is the spirit that quickeneth”: quickeneth means gives life. “The flesh profiteth nothing.” Remember what Christ said to Nicodemus: that which is born of the Spirit is spirit, that which is born of the flesh is flesh. The flesh is sin, and it profits nothing.

“The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” The words Christ spoke unto us are the words of Moses and the prophets. So the words of the Bible, the Bible itself, is the word of life: the words of Moses and the prophets and the apostles and Christ himself are the words of life. That is the spirit you must be born of.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
We are still dealing with what the spirit is. “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.”

“For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” So the laws of God are spiritual. The laws of God going back to Moses and the prophets, and the apostles and Christ himself, are spiritual. They are the spirit that Christ spoke of: the words that are spirit and life.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain.” Mortal men, covered in this flesh, have miserable thoughts, because we always have worries, concerns, trauma, issues, drama, malfunctions, dysfunctions. Our devices are our plans, and they are uncertain. Man plans, God laughs: we can have a plan and God says, no, you’re not doing that, that’s a stupid idea, because our fleshy mind gives us stupid thoughts sometimes.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul.” The corruptible body is this flesh that covers us. That’s why Christ said the spirit quickeneth and the flesh profiteth nothing. “And the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things”: the flesh grows old by the day. Once you’re born, that’s the countdown to your death. You can work out and try to extend it, but it ages regardless; you can’t fight against time. That’s why our forefathers made it clear the best thing to celebrate is death: you get that new body that never dies, doesn’t wither, doesn’t age, and doesn’t weigh you down with miserable thoughts. Paul called this body vile. Our fathers didn’t celebrate birthdays; there was no point when you are born in captivity. That’s why babies cry when they’re born: they know where they’re at. The mind that museth upon many things is a mind all over the place in captivity: bills, car notes, rent, mortgage, kids, clothes.

“And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth”: we have an idea, but we don’t know everything, because we are mortal fleshly men and women. What we do understand, we understand through labour, research, trying to figure it out. “But the things that are in heaven who hath searched out?” The things in heaven go back to this Bible: who has searched out the things in this Bible? “And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above?” To have counsel of what is wisdom, God must send his Holy Spirit from above to you, to understand what was required of you in heaven.

“For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed.” Reformed: remember David said how he was formed in the belly, and Christ told Nicodemus, be born again. It all goes back to when you are born. Reform comes from the Latin, to form again, to shape again: re, again, and form, to form. Reformed is being born again, formed again, remade.

And you can learn a lot from babies, because that is exactly what we become when we repent. When you repent and come into this truth you literally become a newborn all over again. You have to crawl. Your eyes are weak; you can barely see what’s going on, because you’ve been in darkness. Where is the child? In the womb, in darkness. Where were you before you came to the truth? Darkness. It is the exact same thing. When you read the Bible at first you don’t see things clearly, until you develop and grow; then you start to see like a baby sees, and the first thing you do is start drinking the milk.

How are you reformed? “Men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee, and were saved through wisdom.” You are reformed because you are taught the things that please your God, the things searched out in heaven, and saved through wisdom, which is God’s commandments. There are layers behind what Christ said to Nicodemus.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
Read again now: “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.” Now we have an idea what the water is, and what the Spirit is.

Both go back to God’s laws, God’s commandments, and the faith of his Son. That is what Christ was telling Nicodemus: the water and the Spirit you must be born of are the word that washes, “the washing of water by the word.”

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

points: “And men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the foul spirits within them rather than getting right. Paul was open about what he battled, and one of the things the Lord set up the leadership for is the healing of the nation, so we shouldn’t keep things bottled up.

note.label: The Price of Gold

points: “For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light”. The Lord set up leaders many years ago, a lot of them longer than some of us have been alive. Schizophreniform includes social withdrawal, not operating well in social settings, but here it says there’s a foul spirit in you that will make you not come to where Christ is. It’s not you being an introvert. You have to purge the foul spirit from you. When the leaders are in the various cities or in your local city, there are always ones who are there in body but not there in spirit, because what is leading them is the foul spirit that hates the light.

“Lest his deeds should be reproved.” Why do we keep things bottled up inside? Because you don’t want the correction for the foul spirit within you. The light is going to illuminate that spirit, and we don’t want our deeds revealed; we don’t want to deal with the shame and the embarrassment. Why do they always have to bring such and such up? To get your mind right. You better thank the Lord for the righteous smiting you, and count it as the ointment that was upon Aaron’s beard.

note.label: The Price of Gold

points: “But he that doeth truth cometh to the light”. The brothers who want to get right come around. When leadership is at the table going through scriptures, or in the war room, you see brothers asking sincere questions and getting the understanding. And some brothers never come around. You’re trying to hide the foul spirit within you, but when you try to hide it, all you do is illuminate it and make it more obvious.

“That his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” The objective of coming around, despite the correction and the instruction, is that you want it daily. That is what we started with: Christ daily in the temple, and the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits.

note.label: The Price of Gold

points: Many grew up on John 3:16 like a national anthem, and they read verse 16 alone. They accuse us of cherry picking, but they never quote verse 14: “And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up”.
“Even so” means the exact same way and for the exact same reason. The people Moses lifted up the serpent for in the wilderness were Israel, and Christ had to be lifted up for the same people.

Remember too that when Christ walked the earth and taught, there was no Gospel of John and there were no letters of Paul. The gospels are accounts given after he died, rose and went up to glory with his Father. Christ was not quoting John; John was recording what happened.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

points: “That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.” The apologist jumps on “whosoever” and says it means everybody. But the whosoever here is the same people verse 14 is talking about: the people the serpent was lifted up for in the wilderness.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

points: “For God so loved the world”. The same whosoever of verse 15 is the whosoever of verse 16. So the verse is taken apart piece by piece, and the key word is “loved.”

Loved is past tense. I loved that movie: I saw it before. I loved that car: I had it before. So God loved this world before. The question is what world God loved before, and the Old Testament answers it. Nowhere does it say God loved the Moabites or the Canaanites, or that he made a promise to their forefathers. The love and the promise were to Israel’s fathers.

Many who sit in this truth are still covertly thinking the world really means the other nations. The apologists run to the Greek, to Blue Letter Bible and Strong’s, and use the Strong’s to bring forth their strong delusions. So go through the Bible and see whether hatred has made us blind, or whether the Bible itself says who the world is.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

points: The love part is plain; now the world part. The apologists will run to the Greek: the word world in John 3:16 is G2889, kosmos, and its list of meanings includes the inhabitants of the earth, the human family, even the Gentiles as contrasted with the Jews. So, they say, God loved everybody.

But where in the Old Testament, which Christ taught from, can that be found? Christ was not quoting John or Paul or Matthew. The same word kosmos is used for the world in John 1:29, John 3:16 and 17, and John 12:19, so follow it through John and see who the Bible itself calls the world. And Israel is not found anywhere on that list of definitions, or is it?

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

points: “That he gave his only begotten Son”. Is that statement in the Old Testament, that God gave his son? Of course it is, in Isaiah 9. And there the government and the order of the Son’s kingdom answer what the world is.

Go back to the kosmos definitions, and definition number one is an apt and harmonious arrangement or constitution, order, government. That is the world of John 3:16: the government and order of the Israelites, the kingdom Christ establishes on the throne of David. Number one, the first definition, is the right one: not five, not eight.

note.label: GOD SO LOVED THE WORLD

points: Light came into the world, but men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil. Christ is that light: the Messiah, lawkeeper, lawgiver and teacher who magnified God's law. People prefer the darkness because sin is pleasurable. Deliverance from the kingdom of darkness requires turning away from that preference.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

points: “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews”: a man of position.

note.label: The Evolution of Persecution

points: “The same came to Jesus by night”. He came by night. A lot of you want to be on social media telling the world, putting a whole album out saying you’re the Israelite, and now where are you? Sit back, learn, and apply the commandments. Everybody has a position; that is why we have the bishops and deacons. Let them be on the forefront. And brothers who are scared to come to the school: you aren’t doing anything illegal. We read the Bible.

“Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.” Except the Lord was with the leadership, there is no way to go from a basement in Coney Island to over 180 countries visited and hundreds of congregations all over the world. People keep saying that group is just Acts 5. Apply that to the NFAC, around for a good two weeks, but not this organization. This is by God. They said it after Kyrie, they said it after Kanye, and we are still here. We aren’t going anywhere until they kill us.

note.label: The Evolution of Persecution

points: We are that light in a dark place. “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world”: that light is Christ, and they see Christ in us. “And men loved darkness”: men hate it because we are a reflection of what they are not. We are the reflection that the laws of God can be kept, and they hate God’s laws. You Christians hate the law of God. Just be honest.

“Rather than light”: you love your sin rather than coming to Christ. That is what moves them in their spirit to cut Deacon Asaph off, to yell at us, Jesus! Jesus!, instead of saying, these brothers are coming straight out of the Bible, I’m going to believe what God says. They would rather lie and call us a hate group, because they love darkness.

note.label: ACROSS MANY LANDS

points: “Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.” They don’t talk much about his education, but to be a ruler he had position, a seat, like the bourgeois.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God.” We know: all the Pharisees and Herod knew who Christ was, but because of the hatred and evil in their hearts, their love for darkness and their love for Herod, they would not accept him.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God”: unless you are born again, you cannot see the coming kingdom.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit”: the water goes to the word and the spirit goes to the word. All it means is the word of God. Christians interpret it as being dumped in a river. What does being dumped in a river have to do with anything? You just come out a wet crackhead, whatever you were, you’re just wet.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Ye must be born again”: all of us, just as he told Nicodemus, must be born again.

“The wind bloweth where it listeth”: when the word of God travels, it goes where it wants. “And thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” Like this word we are teaching now: we don’t know who online it is touching, who decides to change their life. At camp the person right in front of you might not be the one who repents; it might be the brother or sister way in the back listening who says, I’m going to change my life.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things?” You are a master in Israel and confused about being born again, which means your whole life has to change and start all over.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: The fourth point was the myth of a colorblind society. They do not mean you cannot see color; they want you blind to your own color, your heritage. And they do it through their Christianity, their policies, integration. Now we want to be in their churches and among them, and they hate our guts.

“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” They use that to deceive you into thinking God is colorblind, so everybody has to be around each other. They read John 3:16 and negate Matthew 15:24. Christ was speaking to nobody but his people.

note.label: State of Decay

points: Nicodemus, “a ruler of the Jews”, came to Christ by night. And Christ answered him: “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” The conversation at hand here is being born again. This whole class revolves around being born again, being born of fire and water. What does that mean?

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?” Nicodemus said, what are you talking about, being born again? You are going to climb back into your mother’s womb when you are already grown? Nicodemus had no idea what Christ was talking about.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.” Being born again means being born of water and of the Spirit.

When the class came back to this verse, after the water had been opened up, it came plain: the water is wisdom, God’s laws, and the Spirit is the same. Both the water and the Spirit go back to God’s laws, God’s commandments, and the faith of his Son. That is what Christ is talking about.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.” There is a distinction between the two.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

points: “The wind bloweth where it listeth.” The wind is the word of God. When we go out and bring forth the word of God to our people, we don’t know who is listening, who is being affected by it, who’s listening and who’s not. The Lord doesn’t let us know that, because if we understood where the wind blows it would get to our heads. We would become egotistical, get ahead of ourselves and become arrogant. So the Lord doesn’t allow us to see how large this movement is.

Some Israel say the Israelite movement is a joke and isn’t taken seriously. France says something very different: they outlawed our congregation out there, and if people are caught listening to us they can be fined. If a whole damn government is passing laws on us teaching, someone is taking it seriously. We march through Oakland, California, watched by hundreds and thousands in the street with helicopters flying over us, and there is no news footage. When we marched in the Bronx, a brother who was a reporter and photographer took picture after picture in awe, trying to write an article, and his publisher, an Israeli so-called, said no, don’t put that out there, because they run and control the media. We are blackballed, we are blacklisted. This movement is taken very seriously.

“And thou hearest the sound thereof”: you hear the sound because we are in the street teaching. You hear the mic, the brothers reading aloud with power. Cry loud, spare not. You hear the wind. “But canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit”: those that hear the word.
